trust_decision.summary: The duck-typed buffer test trusts `obj.constructor.isBuffer` to be callable whenever it is truthy, and calls it at lib/utils.js:332; any stringify input carrying an own `constructor` key whose `isBuffer` is a non-callable (a string, number, boolean, array or object, which qs.parse itself can produce under `allowPrototypes`/`plainObjects`) makes that call throw an uncaught TypeError, so a value that is merely data is trusted as a type predicate.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the attacker-controlled `isBuffer`, and `isBuffer` has exactly one definition in the tree (lib/utils.js:327), so grepping the symbol lands there first; the DoS surfaces one file away at the only caller, lib/stringify.js:134.

fix_sites.entry_point: qs.stringify(obj) (lib/index.js:10 -> lib/stringify.js:134) and the exported helper utils.isBuffer (require('qs/lib/utils'), lib/utils.js:375)
fix_sites.module_kind: internal shared utility module (deep-requireable helper, not the package main lib/index.js)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/utils.js:327-333, exported as utils.isBuffer at lib/utils.js:375 and consumed at lib/stringify.js:134

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The throw only manifests inside qs.stringify, and lib/stringify.js:134 is the single in-repo caller of isBuffer, so guarding the call site is sufficient; utils.isBuffer is an internal helper rather than a supported API, and the project's own threat model (.github/THREAT_MODEL.md:28) says stringify input is the caller's own data and not an untrusted channel.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: isBuffer must keep returning true for a callable duck-typed `constructor.isBuffer` (SaferBuffer/Buffer instances) so that qs.stringify({ a: SaferBuffer.from('test') }) still yields 'a=test' (test/stringify.js:929-933, test/utils.js:604-612), and stringify must keep working when the global Buffer is deleted (test/stringify.js:940-948); an over-broad fix such as `Buffer.isBuffer(obj)`, a `typeof obj.constructor === 'function'` test, or a blanket try/catch returning false breaks one of these.

O6_input_shapes: non-callable object with own isBuffer property ({ isBuffer: true })
nested object value ({ b: 'c' }) and array value (['b']) as the isBuffer of a nested constructor key inside stringify
null-prototype objects ({ __proto__: null, constructor: { __proto__: null, isBuffer: 'y' } })
parse round-trip output under plainObjects: true and allowPrototypes: true ('x[constructor][isBuffer]=y')

O7_producer.where: lib/parse.js:390-413 (parseKeys/merge -> utils.setProperty at lib/utils.js:70-81) builds the own `constructor` key when allowPrototypes/plainObjects keep it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The committed standalone browser build dist/qs.js still carries the unguarded expression, so Qs.stringify from the bower/script-tag artifact throws on the same input
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: dist/qs.js is a browserify bundle generated by `npm run dist` (package.json:82) and rebuilt at prepack, so it is an artifact rather than a source site and needs no hand edit
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same repository, one directory away from lib/ (dist/qs.js vs lib/utils.js); no other package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second duck-typed type check applied to the same value, e.g. `utils.isTypedArray(obj)` implemented as `obj.constructor.isTypedArray(obj)` beside the isBuffer test
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: isBuffer exists only because browserified Buffer shims differ and Buffer may be absent (test/stringify.js:940-948), so adding typed-array or DataView support the same duck-typed way is the style a maintainer here would reach for

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse accepting a caller-supplied object input and calling utils.isBuffer on its values, a second call site of the same helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parse already takes a non-string input object at lib/parse.js:397 (`typeof str === 'string' ? parseValues(str, options) : str`), so preserving buffers through parse by calling utils.isBuffer on its values is a natural, small addition

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling duck-typed predicate next to isRegExp that invokes a value's own constructor property, e.g. `obj.constructor.isRegExp(obj)`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: lib/utils.js already collects small type predicates invoked on caller data (isRegExp is used at lib/parse.js:374), so copying the isBuffer duck-typing pattern in the same file is plausible

O9_family: Improper check / uncaught exception in a duck-typed type test (CWE-248, CWE-703) leading to denial of service when attacker-controlled data is used as a type predicate

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js (package.json:30 engines node >=0.6) and npm; tape + nyc for tests, eslint + evalmd in pretest, browserify for the dist bundle
O10_build.project_tests: tape suites under test/ run by `npm run tests-only` (`nyc tape 'test/**/*.js'`, package.json:77); the relevant ones are test/utils.js:597 (isBuffer), test/stringify.js:929-933 (buffer values, the must-keep-working case) and test/stringify.js:940-948 (Buffer global deleted); `npm test` also runs eslint/evalmd and a network `npx npm audit` posttest, so use tests-only offline

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap or gate the isBuffer call at lib/stringify.js:134 (try/catch, or `Buffer.isBuffer(obj)`) so stringify stops throwing, leaving utils.isBuffer itself and the dist bundle unchanged.

unverified: Repository size in MB: no shell access, so only the source shape is evidenced — lib/ is four files totalling ~1,180 lines (lib/utils.js:1-381, lib/stringify.js:1-378, lib/parse.js:1-414, lib/index.js:1-11) plus one bundled dist/qs.js; the logos/ assets dominate the tree and were not measured.

Whether the hidden behavioural tests exercise dist/qs.js: no file under test/ references dist, so an unfixed bundle would still pass the project's own suite; the dist route may carry no scoring signal.

Whether `utils.isBuffer` counts as a public entry point: it is exported at lib/utils.js:375 and tested directly via require('../lib/utils') at test/utils.js:9 and test/utils.js:597, but package.json:13 makes lib/index.js the package main, so O1 = 2 assumes the deep-require surface counts.
Whether dist/qs.js is regenerated (and therefore fixed) in a later release commit: no latest release was provided, so the O8 latest_where is unknown.
